summary: Pointer-surgery problems. Two tools solve most of them: a dummy head (so inserting/deleting the first node needs no special case) and the fast/slow pointer (middle, cycle detection, palindrome, nth-from-end). Merge-sort is the O(N log N) way to sort a list; LRU cache pairs a HashMap with a doubly linked list for O(1) get/put.

thoughtProcess.title: Editing near the head? Use a dummy node.
thoughtProcess.body: dummy.next = head; work with a 'prev' pointer starting at dummy; return dummy.next. This removes the special case for changing the first element.

thoughtProcess.title: Middle / cycle / palindrome / nth-from-end -> fast & slow pointers.
thoughtProcess.body: slow moves 1, fast moves 2. When fast hits the end, slow is at the middle. If fast ever meets slow, there is a cycle (Floyd).

thoughtProcess.title: Always cache node.next before you rewire it.
thoughtProcess.body: Reversing or reordering overwrites next; save it in a temp first or you lose the rest of the list.

keyPatterns.name: Dummy head
keyPatterns.when: Insert/delete/partition where the head may change
keyPatterns.template: ListNode dummy=new ListNode(0); dummy.next=head; ListNode prev=dummy; ... return dummy.next;

keyPatterns.name: Merge two sorted lists
keyPatterns.template: walk both with a dummy tail, attach the smaller head each step, append the leftover

keyPatterns.name: HashMap + doubly linked list
keyPatterns.template: map key->node; DLL orders by recency; on access move node to front; evict from tail when full

commonMistakes.title: Losing the rest of the list while rewiring
commonMistakes.wrong: cur.next = prev; cur = cur.next; // cur.next already changed
commonMistakes.right: ListNode nxt = cur.next; cur.next = prev; prev = cur; cur = nxt;
commonMistakes.why: Once you set cur.next you can't reach the old successor — cache it first.

commonMistakes.title: Missing null / single-node checks
commonMistakes.why: Dereferencing next on a null or last node throws NullPointerException; guard both fast and fast.next.

edgeCases: Empty list (head == null) and single node — most routines should return immediately.
Even vs odd length changes which node fast/slow lands on for 'middle' — pick the convention the problem wants.
Cycle present: a naive traversal loops forever; detect with Floyd before length/print operations.
Add-two-numbers: carry can remain after both lists end — append a final node when carry != 0.
